_reference_titles_source: VERIFIED live via tools/yt_research.py 2026-08-02 (--query 'amish home hack,old farmhouse trick,grandmothers home remedy,no ac cooling trick without power' --window all --long-only). Confirms the original (2026-07-31, saved-to-repo-late) titles were real: 2 of the 4 original entries showed up again independently as top-vpd hits. Raw data: docs/research/home-hacks.json / .txt. NEW pattern spotted that the current title formula doesn't cover: multi-hack LISTICLE titles ('35 Hydrogen Peroxide Hacks', '25 BANNED Hacks from the 60s') are now a strong recurring shape alongside the single-hack formula - consider adding a listicle variant to title.ingredients if a future video wants to batch several small fixes instead of one deep one. Runtime confirms the niche: 30d/365d medians both ~25-27 min, squarely inside the existing [12,30] target range - no change needed there.

title.formula: [cheap number anchor] + [absolute quantifier] + [negation stack] + [borrowed authority] + [parenthetical payoff]

negation_stack: No Air Conditioner. No Fan. No Power Needed.

rules: Lead with the cheap number - it is the whole promise. VALIDATED 2026-08-02 by tools/yt_viral_analyze.py: a dollar anchor in the title correlated with breaking out in 53% of cases (10 of 19 videos) against a 33% baseline - the best-powered lever signal found across all 5 niches. This rule was originally written from a growth-coach's advice; it now has this channel's own outlier data behind it.

Borrowed authority (Amish / grandma / Depression-era) is TABLE STAKES, not an edge - measured 2026-08-02 at a 31% breakout rate against a 33% baseline, i.e. it performs exactly at par. Use it to compete, but never expect it to be the thing that makes a video travel; the number anchor and the contrarian turn (45%, 5 of 11) are what actually separate.
The negation stack pre-kills objections; use 2-3 short negations, not a sentence.

Borrowed authority beats personal authority in TITLE COPY in this niche - lean on 'Old Farmhouse/Depression-era/Grandmother's', not on naming the narrator. (Updated 2026-08-03: the channel now has a face - narrator persona 'Walt Combs', see channel-persona.home-hacks.json - but that's the on-screen avatar, not a title-copy lever; this rule about titles stands.)
Never use a question as the title. This audience wants a claim, not a puzzle.

structure.note: State the payoff in the first 10 seconds, plainly. No channel intro, no 'welcome back'.
What it costs them to keep doing it the current way. Money, health, comfort. Concrete numbers.
The borrowed-authority origin story. Where this trick comes from and why it was forgotten.
The actual steps, numbered, slow, repeated. This is the bulk. One idea per beat.
Answer the doubts out loud: does it smell, is it safe, will it work in humidity, does it need power.
Small rooms, big rooms, apartments, garages. Extends watch time honestly.
Recap the numbers, one soft CTA. No hard sell.

voice_rules: Short sentences. One clause. This audience is often half-listening while doing something else.
Repeat the key number at least 4 times across the video.
No hedging: 'this works', not 'this may help'. But never invent a fact to achieve that.
script.honesty_guard: This niche rewards overclaiming, which is how channels get demonetised and sued. Every number in the script must be defensible. If a claim cannot be supported, soften the claim - do not fabricate a source.

images.style: warm, domestic, natural light, lived-in American home, no people's faces, no modern tech

sound._bed_gain_note: Corrected 2026-07-30 (was -16, never measured). docu-pluck's own mean is -22.4dB; -16 put the effective bed near -38dB, inaudible against a ~-25dB speech-gap floor. -5 lands it at the validated -27dB target. Re-derive if the bed clip changes: bed_gain_db = -27 - <clip's measured mean dB>.
